# SEO-022: Enforce a single trailing-slash form per path

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Domain | `urls` |

| Change safety | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` |
| Evidence tier | `A` |
| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

For every public path, one of the slash-terminated and non-slash-terminated forms serves the content and the other returns a permanent redirect to it. Both forms never return 200 for the same resource.

## Rationale

Two forms of the same path both answering with content produce a duplicate for every page on the site, which halves the link signal reaching each one and doubles the number of URLs a crawler has to fetch.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site",
    "has_router"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Determine which form the framework or host already emits by default and adopt it rather than fighting it. Configure the single normalization rule at the routing or edge layer, then confirm internal links, the sitemap, and canonical values all use the chosen form.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Request a representative path in both slash forms and record which one returns content and which one redirects, with the status code.
- Evidence: `REDIRECT_CHAIN`, `HTTP_STATUS`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
